records.source: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב רַגְלָ֑יו וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אַ֥רְצָה בְנֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃
records.gloss: And lifted up Jacob his feet and went to [the] land of [the] sons of [the] east.
pieces: Jacob went on his way and came to the land of the eastern peoples.

L.1: And Jacob lifted up his feet and went to the land of the people of the east.

R.1: Jacob continued his trip and came to the land of the people of the east.

decisions.choice: lifted up his feet: set off, went on his way
decisions.reason: The expression occurs only here. It may simply mean that Jacob set out, or suggest that he went on with fresh heart after God's promise at Bethel (28:15).

decisions.choice: the people of the east: the peoples beyond the Jordan and the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The people of the east" (benei qedem) is a general name for the tribes east of Canaan (Judges 6:3; Job 1:3). Here it is the region of Haran (verse 4).

decisions.choice: went on his way (B); continued his trip (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m1).

records.source: וַיַּ֞רְא וְהִנֵּ֧ה בְאֵ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּה־שָׁ֞ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עֶדְרֵי־צֹאן֙ רֹבְצִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֚י מִן־הַבְּאֵ֣ר הַהִ֔וא יַשְׁק֖וּ הָעֲדָרִ֑ים וְהָאֶ֥בֶן גְּדֹלָ֖ה עַל־פִּ֥י הַבְּאֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And he looked, and look, a well in the field, and look, there three flocks of sheep [were] lying beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks; and the stone [was] large over [the] mouth of the well.
pieces: There he saw a well out in the open country, with three flocks of sheep lying beside it, because the flocks were watered from that well. A big stone covered the opening of the well.

L.2: And he looked, and look, [there was] a well in the field, and look, three flocks of sheep were lying there beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks. And the stone over the mouth of the well was large.

R.2: He saw a well in a field. Three flocks of sheep were lying near it, because the shepherds got water for their sheep from that well. There was a big stone over the top of the well.

decisions.choice: a well: where wives are found
decisions.reason: Abraham's servant found Rebekah at a well near this same town (24:11-15), and Moses will meet his wife at a well (Exodus 2:15-21). The reader expects a meeting.

decisions.choice: the stone was large: a cover to protect the water
decisions.reason: A heavy stone kept the well clean and kept anyone from drawing water alone. By local custom it was moved only when all the shepherds had gathered (verses 3, 8).

records.source: וְנֶאֶסְפוּ־שָׁ֣מָּה כָל־הָעֲדָרִ֗ים וְגָלֲל֤וּ אֶת־הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וְהִשְׁק֖וּ אֶת־הַצֹּ֑אן וְהֵשִׁ֧יבוּ אֶת־הָאֶ֛בֶן עַל־פִּ֥י הַבְּאֵ֖ר לִמְקֹמָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And they would gather there all the flocks, and they would roll the stone from over [the] mouth of the well and water the sheep, and put back the stone over [the] mouth of the well in its place.
pieces: The custom was that when all the flocks had gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone off the well's opening and water the sheep, and then put the stone back in place over the opening.

L.3: And all the flocks would be gathered there, and they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and put the stone back in its place over the mouth of the well.

R.3: When all the flocks came together, the shepherds would roll the stone away and give water to the sheep. Then they would put the stone back over the well.

decisions.choice: would gather ... would roll: what was usually done
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe a regular practice, not one event: this is how the well was always used.

decisions.choice: the shepherds
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who did the work, as verse 8 makes clear.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב אַחַ֖י מֵאַ֣יִן אַתֶּ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵחָרָ֖ן אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And said to them Jacob, my brothers, from where [are] you? And they said, from Haran [are] we.
pieces: "Friends, where are you from?" Jacob asked them. "From Haran," they answered.

L.4: And Jacob said to them, "My brothers, where are you from?" And they said, "We are from Haran."

R.4: Jacob asked the shepherds, "My friends, where do you come from?" They answered, "We are from Haran."

decisions.choice: my brothers: a friendly greeting to strangers
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is a courteous address, not a claim of kinship.

decisions.choice: Friends (B); My friends (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the friendly greeting (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם הַיְדַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־לָבָ֣ן בֶּן־נָח֑וֹר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יָדָֽעְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, do you know Laban, son of Nahor? And they said, we know [him].
pieces: "Do you know Laban, Nahor's grandson?" he asked. "Yes, we know him," they said.

L.5: And he said to them, "Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?" And they said, "We know [him]."

R.5: Jacob asked them, "Do you know Laban, the grandson of Nahor?" They answered, "Yes, we know him."

decisions.choice: the son of Nahor: Nahor's descendant
decisions.reason: Laban was the son of Bethuel and grandson of Nahor, Abraham's brother (24:15, 29). "Son" often means a descendant, and Nahor was the head of the family.

decisions.choice: grandson
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the relationship as it was (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָהֶ֖ם הֲשָׁל֣וֹם ל֑וֹ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ שָׁל֔וֹם וְהִנֵּה֙ רָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ בָּאָ֖ה עִם־הַצֹּֽאן׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, [is there] peace to him? And they said, peace; and look, Rachel his daughter [is] coming with the sheep.
pieces: "Is he well?" he asked. "He is," they replied, "and here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep now."

L.6: And he said to them, "Is it well with him?" And they said, "[It is] well; and look, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep."

R.6: Jacob asked, "Is he well?" They said, "Yes, he is. Look, here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep."

decisions.choice: is it well with him? (hashalom lo): the usual greeting
decisions.reason: To ask after someone's shalom is to ask about their health and welfare (43:27).

decisions.choice: Rachel: "ewe"
decisions.reason: The name means a female sheep. Rachel first appears as a shepherd with her father's flock (verse 9).

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֵ֥ן עוֹד֙ הַיּ֣וֹם גָּד֔וֹל לֹא־עֵ֖ת הֵאָסֵ֣ף הַמִּקְנֶ֑ה הַשְׁק֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן וּלְכ֥וּ רְעֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said, look, still the day [is] great; not [is it the] time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and go, pasture [them].
pieces: "But it is the middle of the day," Jacob said, "far too early to bring the animals in. Why not water the sheep and take them back to graze?"

L.7: And he said, "Look, it is still high day; it is not time for the livestock to be gathered. Water the sheep and go, pasture [them]."

R.7: Jacob said, "It is still the middle of the day. It is not time yet to bring the animals in for the night. Give the sheep some water. Then take them back out to eat grass."

decisions.choice: the day is still great: it is broad daylight
decisions.reason: Much of the day is left. Jacob, a skilled herdsman, sees no reason for the flocks to wait idle; he may also want the shepherds gone before Rachel arrives.

decisions.choice: Why not water the sheep ...?
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the stranger's command as a suggestion, which is how it would be heard.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ לֹ֣א נוּכַל֒ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֲדָרִ֔ים וְגָֽלֲלוּ֙ אֶת־הָאֶ֔בֶן מֵעַ֖ל פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֑ר וְהִשְׁקִ֖ינוּ הַצֹּֽאן׃
records.gloss: And they said, not we are able, until are gathered all the flocks and they roll the stone from over [the] mouth of the well; then we water the sheep.
pieces: "We are not allowed to," they answered, "until all the flocks have come in and the stone has been rolled off the well. Then we can water the sheep."

L.8: And they said, "We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we water the sheep."

R.8: They answered, "We cannot do that until all the flocks are here. Then the stone is rolled away, and we give water to the sheep."

decisions.choice: we cannot: it is not done, or not possible
decisions.reason: The shepherds may mean that custom forbids it, or that the stone is too heavy for a few of them. Jacob then moves it alone (verse 10).

records.source: עוֹדֶ֖נּוּ מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֑ם וְרָחֵ֣ל׀בָּ֗אָה עִם־הַצֹּאן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יהָ כִּ֥י רֹעָ֖ה הִֽוא׃
records.gloss: Still he [was] speaking with them, and Rachel came with the sheep that [belonged] to her father, for a shepherdess [was] she.
pieces: He was still talking with them when Rachel arrived with her father's sheep, since she was the one who looked after them.

L.9: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

R.9: While Jacob was still talking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep. She took care of them.

decisions.choice: a shepherdess: a daughter tending the family flock
decisions.reason: Daughters often helped with the flocks (Exodus 2:16). The word is the feminine of the ordinary word for shepherd.

records.source: וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ רָאָ֨ה יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־רָחֵ֗ל בַּת־לָבָן֙ אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֔וֹ וְאֶת־צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֣שׁ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַיָּ֤גֶל אֶת־הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיַּ֕שְׁקְ אֶת־צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was, when saw Jacob Rachel, daughter of Laban, brother of his mother, and [the] sheep of Laban, brother of his mother, and drew near Jacob and rolled the stone from over [the] mouth of the well and watered [the] sheep of Laban, brother of his mother.
pieces: When Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his uncle Laban, with Laban's sheep, he stepped forward, rolled the stone off the well's opening by himself, and watered his uncle's flock.

L.10: And when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, Jacob went up and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well and watered the sheep of Laban his mother's brother.

R.10: Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother's brother Laban, with Laban's sheep. He went to the well and rolled the stone away by himself. Then he gave water to Laban's sheep.

decisions.choice: his mother's brother: three times in one verse
decisions.reason: The repetition shows what fills Jacob's mind: these are his mother's people, the family he was sent to (28:2).

decisions.choice: rolled the stone: alone, against custom
decisions.reason: Jacob does by himself what the shepherds said needed all of them (verse 8). It shows his strength and his eagerness, and it serves Rachel as Rebekah once served Abraham's servant at a well (24:18-20).

decisions.choice: by himself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out what the context shows (verses 3, 8).

records.source: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק יַעֲקֹ֖ב לְרָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ׃
records.gloss: And kissed Jacob Rachel, and he lifted up his voice and wept.
pieces: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and broke into loud weeping.

L.11: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice and wept.

R.11: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and began to cry out loud.

decisions.choice: kissed: a greeting between relatives
decisions.reason: A kiss was the normal greeting within a family (verse 13; 33:4). Jacob greets his cousin before telling her who he is (verse 12).

decisions.choice: lifted up his voice and wept: wept aloud
decisions.reason: After a long and lonely journey Jacob has reached his mother's family. He weeps from relief and joy.

records.source: וַיַּגֵּ֨ד יַעֲקֹ֜ב לְרָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י אֲחִ֤י אָבִ֨יהָ֙ ה֔וּא וְכִ֥י בֶן־רִבְקָ֖ה ה֑וּא וַתָּ֖רָץ וַתַּגֵּ֥ד לְאָבִֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And told Jacob to Rachel that [the] relative of her father [was] he, and that [the] son of Rebekah [was] he. And she ran and told her father.
pieces: He explained to Rachel that he was a relative of her father, Rebekah's son, and she ran off to tell her father.

L.12: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's relative, and that he was Rebekah's son; and she ran and told her father.

R.12: Jacob told Rachel that he was part of her father's family. He was Rebekah's son. Rachel ran and told her father.

decisions.choice: her father's relative: literally "her father's brother"
decisions.reason: "Brother" (ach) is used for any close kinsman, as Abraham called Lot his brother (13:8; 14:14). Jacob was Laban's nephew.

decisions.choice: relative
decisions.reason: The general sense of the word is given (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ לָבָ֜ן אֶת־שֵׁ֣מַע׀יַעֲקֹ֣ב בֶּן־אֲחֹת֗וֹ וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיְחַבֶּק־לוֹ֙ וַיְנַשֶּׁק־ל֔וֹ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר לְלָבָ֔ן אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And it was, when heard Laban [the] report of Jacob, son of his sister, and he ran to meet him and embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house; and he recounted to Laban all these things.
pieces: As soon as Laban heard about Jacob, his sister's son, he ran out to meet him, hugged and kissed him, and took him home. Jacob told Laban everything that had happened.

L.13: And when Laban heard the news of Jacob his sister's son, he ran to meet him and embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.

R.13: When Laban heard that his sister's son Jacob was there, he ran out to meet him. He hugged him and kissed him and brought him to his home. Jacob told Laban all about what had happened.

decisions.choice: he ran ... embraced ... kissed ... brought him to his house: Laban's warm welcome
decisions.reason: Laban had run out to meet Abraham's servant once he saw the gold given to Rebekah (24:29-31). Jacob comes with no camels or gifts; how Laban treats him will soon be seen.

decisions.choice: all these things: Jacob's story
decisions.reason: What Jacob told is not said: probably his journey and why he came, perhaps also what happened with Esau.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ לָבָ֔ן אַ֛ךְ עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עִמּ֖וֹ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said to him Laban, surely my bone and my flesh [are] you. And he stayed with him a month of days.
pieces: "You really are my own bone and flesh!" Laban said to him. Jacob stayed on with him for a whole month.

L.14: And Laban said to him, "Surely you are my bone and my flesh!" And he stayed with him a full month.

R.14: Laban said to him, "You really are part of my own family!" Jacob stayed with Laban for a month.

decisions.choice: my bone and my flesh: my own family
decisions.reason: The phrase means close kin (Judges 9:2; 2 Samuel 5:1). It echoes the man's words about the woman in 2:23.

decisions.choice: a month of days: a full month
decisions.reason: The phrase means a whole month, a period of hospitality after which questions of work and wages arise (verse 15).

decisions.choice: part of my own family
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the expression (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב הֲכִי־אָחִ֣י אַ֔תָּה וַעֲבַדְתַּ֖נִי חִנָּ֑ם הַגִּ֥ידָה לִּ֖י מַה־מַּשְׂכֻּרְתֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Laban to Jacob, is it because my relative [are] you that you should serve me for nothing? Tell me, what [will be] your wages?
pieces: Then Laban said to Jacob, "You are my relative, but that is no reason for you to work for me without pay. Tell me what you want to be paid."

L.15: And Laban said to Jacob, "Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?"

R.15: Then Laban said to Jacob, "You are my relative, but you should not have to work for me for nothing. Tell me what I should pay you."

decisions.choice: serve me for nothing: the start of a long bargain
decisions.reason: Laban speaks generously, but it makes Jacob a hired worker. The word "wages" returns when Jacob complains that Laban changed his wages ten times (31:7, 41).

decisions.choice: my relative: literally "my brother"
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, "brother" means a kinsman.

records.source: וּלְלָבָ֖ן שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֑וֹת שֵׁ֤ם הַגְּדֹלָה֙ לֵאָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַקְּטַנָּ֖ה רָחֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And to Laban [were] two daughters; [the] name of the older [was] Leah, and [the] name of the younger [was] Rachel.
pieces: Laban had two daughters. The elder was called Leah, and the younger Rachel.

L.16: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

R.16: Laban had two daughters. The older one was named Leah, and the younger one was named Rachel.

decisions.choice: the older ... the younger: the same words as for Esau and Jacob
decisions.reason: The words are "the big one" and "the small one", as used of Esau and Jacob (27:1, 15). Jacob, the younger who took the older's place, will meet the same question in reverse (verse 26).

decisions.choice: Leah: perhaps "cow"
decisions.reason: The name may mean "wild cow" or come from a word for weariness. Like Rachel ("ewe"), it may be a name from herding life.

records.source: וְעֵינֵ֥י לֵאָ֖ה רַכּ֑וֹת וְרָחֵל֙ הָֽיְתָ֔ה יְפַת־תֹּ֖אַר וִיפַ֥ת מַרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] eyes of Leah [were] weak, but Rachel was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance.
pieces: Leah's eyes were delicate, but Rachel was shapely and lovely to look at.

L.17: And Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and beautiful in appearance.

R.17: Leah had gentle eyes, but Rachel was very beautiful in both face and body.

decisions.choice: Leah's eyes were weak (rakkot): soft, tender, or dull
decisions.reason: The word (rakh) means soft or tender. It may be praise (gentle, lovely eyes) or point to eyes without sparkle. The contrast with Rachel suggests Leah's looks were plain beside her sister's.

decisions.choice: beautiful in form and appearance: beautiful in figure and face
decisions.reason: The same pair of words is later used of Joseph, Rachel's son (39:6).

decisions.choice: delicate (B); gentle (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable choose words that keep the uncertainty of the Hebrew (m1).

records.source: וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־רָחֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶֽעֱבָדְךָ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים בְּרָחֵ֥ל בִּתְּךָ֖ הַקְּטַנָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And loved Jacob Rachel, and he said, I will serve you seven years for Rachel your daughter, the younger.
pieces: Jacob had fallen in love with Rachel, so he said, "I will work for you seven years in return for your younger daughter Rachel."

L.18: And Jacob loved Rachel, and he said, "I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter."

R.18: Jacob was in love with Rachel. So he said to Laban, "I will work for you for seven years if you will let me marry your younger daughter Rachel."

decisions.choice: seven years for Rachel: work in place of a bride-price
decisions.reason: A bridegroom normally paid the bride's family a price or gifts (24:53; 34:12). Jacob arrived with nothing, so he offers his labor instead. Seven years' work was a very high price.

decisions.choice: your younger daughter: Jacob makes it plain
decisions.reason: Jacob names her and calls her the younger, as if to leave no room for a mistake. Laban will find one anyway (verse 26).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֗ן ט֚וֹבתִּתִּ֣י אֹתָ֣הּ לָ֔ךְ מִתִּתִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ לְאִ֣ישׁ אַחֵ֑ר שְׁבָ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Laban, better [is] my giving her to you than my giving her to another man; stay with me.
pieces: "Better that she should go to you than to some other man," Laban answered. "Stay here with me."

L.19: And Laban said, "It is better that I give her to you than that I give her to another man; stay with me."

R.19: Laban said, "It is better for me to give her to you than to someone else. Stay here with me."

decisions.choice: it is better that I give her to you: an answer that promises less than it seems
decisions.reason: Laban never says "I will give you Rachel". His careful words leave room for what he does in verse 23.

decisions.choice: than to another man: marriage within the family preferred
decisions.reason: It was thought better for a daughter to marry a kinsman than an outsider (24:3-4; 28:2).

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ד יַעֲקֹ֛ב בְּרָחֵ֖ל שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וַיִּהְי֤וּ בְעֵינָיו֙ כְּיָמִ֣ים אֲחָדִ֔ים בְּאַהֲבָת֖וֹ אֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And served Jacob for Rachel seven years, and they were in his eyes like a few days because of his love for her.
pieces: So Jacob worked seven years to win Rachel, and because he loved her so much, the years went by for him as if they were only a few days.

L.20: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they were in his eyes like a few days, because of his love for her.

R.20: So Jacob worked seven years so he could marry Rachel. He loved her so much that the seven years felt like only a few days.

decisions.choice: a few days: the words Rebekah had used
decisions.reason: Rebekah told Jacob to stay with Laban "a few days" (27:44). The days became years, but love made them seem short.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֤ב אֶל־לָבָן֙ הָבָ֣ה אֶת־אִשְׁתִּ֔י כִּ֥י מָלְא֖וּ יָמָ֑י וְאָב֖וֹאָה אֵלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And said Jacob to Laban, give my wife, for are fulfilled my days, that I may go in to her.
pieces: Then Jacob said to Laban, "My time is up. Give me my wife, so that I may sleep with her."

L.21: And Jacob said to Laban, "Give [me] my wife, for my days are completed, that I may go in to her."

R.21: Then Jacob said to Laban, "I have worked the seven years we agreed on. Now give me Rachel to be my wife so I can live with her as her husband."

decisions.choice: my days are completed: my time of service is over
decisions.reason: The agreed seven years are finished (verse 18).

decisions.choice: my wife: Rachel was already pledged to him
decisions.reason: Once a marriage was agreed, the woman could be called the man's wife before the wedding (Deuteronomy 22:23-24).

decisions.choice: go in to her: consummate the marriage
decisions.reason: To "go in to" a woman is a plain way of speaking of sexual union (16:2; 30:3).

decisions.choice: Rachel
decisions.reason: Readable names the wife Jacob means, which matters for verse 25.

records.source: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף לָבָ֛ן אֶת־כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And gathered Laban all [the] men of the place and made a feast.
pieces: So Laban invited all the {{gender:people|men}} of the place and gave a wedding feast.

L.22: And Laban gathered together all the {{gender:people|men}} of the place and made a feast.

R.22: So Laban invited all the {{gender:people|men}} who lived there to a wedding feast.

decisions.choice: a feast (mishteh): a wedding banquet with wine
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to drink". A wedding feast could last a week (verse 27; Judges 14:12, 17). Wine and darkness help Laban's plan.

decisions.choice: people (default), men (alternative)
decisions.reason: Anshei hammaqom is the population of the place in general, so the gender setting applies.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־לֵאָ֣ה בִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ אֵלָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And it was in the evening, and he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her.
pieces: But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob, and Jacob slept with her.

L.23: And in the evening he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her.

R.23: But that night Laban took his daughter Leah to Jacob instead of Rachel, and Jacob slept with her.

decisions.choice: in the evening: the bride brought veiled, in the dark
decisions.reason: A bride was veiled when she came to her husband (24:65). In the dark, after the feast, Jacob did not know which daughter he had been given.

decisions.choice: he took Leah: the deceiver deceived
decisions.reason: Jacob, who deceived his blind father in the dark of his eyes (27:18-24), is deceived in the dark of night. The narrator makes no comment; the pattern speaks for itself.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since Laban and Jacob are both "he" in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: instead of Rachel
decisions.reason: Readable makes the deception explicit.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לָ֔הּ אֶת־זִלְפָּ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ לְלֵאָ֥ה בִתּ֖וֹ שִׁפְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: And gave Laban to her Zilpah his slave woman, to Leah his daughter [as] a slave woman.
pieces: (Laban had given his servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah, to be her servant.)

L.24: And Laban gave Zilpah his slave woman to his daughter Leah as her slave woman.

R.24: (Laban gave his servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah to be her servant.)

decisions.choice: Zilpah ... as a slave woman (shifchah): part of the bride's dowry
decisions.reason: A father might give his daughter a female slave at her marriage, as Rebekah went with her nurse and her young women (24:59, 61). The slave belonged to the wife, and later bore children for her (30:9-10).

decisions.choice: in parentheses
decisions.reason: The verse is an aside that interrupts the story of the wedding night; Balanced and Readable mark it as such.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m1) keeps that she was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּה־הִ֖וא לֵאָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־לָבָ֗ן מַה־זֹּאת֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לִּ֔י הֲלֹ֤א בְרָחֵל֙ עָבַ֣דְתִּי עִמָּ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה רִמִּיתָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And it was in the morning, and look, she [was] Leah. And he said to Laban, what [is] this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel I served with you? And why have you deceived me?
pieces: In the light of morning Jacob saw that it was Leah. "What have you done to me?" he said to Laban. "It was Rachel I worked for! Why have you tricked me?"

L.25: And in the morning, look, it was Leah! And he said to Laban, "What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I served with you? Why then have you deceived me?"

R.25: In the morning Jacob saw that it was Leah! He said to Laban, "What have you done to me? I worked for you to marry Rachel! Why did you trick me?"

decisions.choice: and look, it was Leah!: the discovery seen through Jacob's eyes
decisions.reason: Hinneh lets the reader share Jacob's shock at daylight.

decisions.choice: deceived me (rimmitani): the same root as "deceit" in 27:35
decisions.reason: Isaac said Jacob came "with deceit" (mirmah) to take Esau's blessing. Now Jacob accuses Laban of the very thing, in a word from the same root.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֔ן לֹא־יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן בִּמְקוֹמֵ֑נוּ לָתֵ֥ת הַצְּעִירָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַבְּכִירָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Laban, not it is done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
pieces: "It is not our custom here," Laban replied, "to give the younger daughter in marriage before the firstborn.

L.26: And Laban said, "It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.

R.26: Laban answered, "Here in our country we do not let the younger daughter marry before the older one.

decisions.choice: the younger before the firstborn: Jacob's own deed turned back on him
decisions.reason: Laban uses the word "firstborn" (bekhirah), the root of the birthright Jacob took from his older brother (25:31-34). Jacob put the younger before the firstborn at home; in Haran it is not done.

decisions.choice: it is not done so in our place: an appeal to local custom
decisions.reason: Laban appeals to custom, but he had agreed to Jacob's terms without mentioning it (verses 18-19).

records.source: מַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את וְנִתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ גַּם־אֶת־זֹ֗את בַּעֲבֹדָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמָּדִ֔י ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע־שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Complete [the] week of this one, and we will give to you also this one, for [the] service that you will serve with me yet seven years other.
pieces: Finish out this one's wedding week, and then we will give you the other one too, in return for another seven years of work for me."

L.27: Complete the week of this one, and we will give you the other also, for the service that you will serve with me for another seven years."

R.27: Spend this week celebrating your marriage to Leah. Then we will give you Rachel too. But you must work for me seven more years."

decisions.choice: complete the week of this one: the week of wedding celebrations
decisions.reason: A wedding feast lasted seven days (Judges 14:12). Jacob must keep Leah's week as her husband before he is given Rachel.

decisions.choice: another seven years: Rachel given at once, the work paid afterward
decisions.reason: Rachel is given after the week (verse 28); the second seven years of work follow (verse 30).

decisions.choice: Leah ... Rachel
decisions.reason: Readable names the two sisters for clarity.

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יַעֲקֹב֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיְמַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את וַיִּתֶּן־ל֛וֹ אֶת־רָחֵ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And did Jacob so and completed [the] week of this one, and he gave to him Rachel his daughter to him as a wife.
pieces: Jacob agreed, and when Leah's week was over, Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.

L.28: And Jacob did so, and completed her week; and he gave him Rachel his daughter as wife.

R.28: Jacob agreed. When the week was over, Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to be his wife too.

decisions.choice: Rachel as wife: two sisters married to one man
decisions.reason: The later Law forbade a man to marry his wife's sister while she lived, as a rival to her (Leviticus 18:18). The rivalry between the sisters fills the chapters that follow (30:1-24).

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לְרָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ אֶת־בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ לָ֖הּ לְשִׁפְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: And gave Laban to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his slave woman, to her as a slave woman.
pieces: (Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel, to be her servant.)

L.29: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his slave woman, to be her slave woman.

R.29: (Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel to be her servant.)

decisions.choice: Bilhah as a slave woman: Rachel's dowry
decisions.reason: As with Zilpah and Leah (verse 24). Bilhah will later bear sons for Rachel (30:3-8) and be the mother of Dan and Naphtali.

decisions.choice: in parentheses
decisions.reason: As in verse 24, the verse is an aside.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m1) keeps that she was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיָּבֹא֙ גַּ֣ם אֶל־רָחֵ֔ל וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב גַּֽם־אֶת־רָחֵ֖ל מִלֵּאָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמּ֔וֹ ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע־שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And he went in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah; and he served with him yet seven years other.
pieces: Jacob slept with Rachel as well, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. And he worked for Laban seven more years.

L.30: And he went in to Rachel also, and he loved Rachel more than Leah; and he served with him another seven years.

R.30: Jacob slept with Rachel too, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. He worked for Laban for seven more years.

decisions.choice: he loved Rachel more than Leah: the favoritism repeats
decisions.reason: Isaac loved Esau, and Rebekah loved Jacob (25:28). Now Jacob loves one wife more, and later one son more (37:3). Each time it brings pain to the family.

decisions.choice: Laban
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one Jacob worked for.

records.source: וַיַּ֤רְא יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־שְׂנוּאָ֣ה לֵאָ֔ה וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־רַחְמָ֑הּ וְרָחֵ֖ל עֲקָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And saw YHWH that [was] hated Leah, and he opened her womb; but Rachel [was] barren.
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that Leah was unloved, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let her conceive, while Rachel remained childless.

L.31: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that Leah was hated, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.

R.31: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw that Jacob did not love Leah as he loved Rachel. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made it possible for Leah to have children. But Rachel could not have children.

decisions.choice: hated (senu'ah): loved less, not favored
decisions.reason: In matters of marriage, "hated" can mean the less favored of two wives (Deuteronomy 21:15-17). Verse 30 says Jacob loved Rachel "more", so Leah was loved less. To Leah it felt like being hated (verse 33).

decisions.choice: the LORD saw ... and opened her womb: God cares for the neglected
decisions.reason: As God saw Hagar in her misery (16:13), he sees Leah. Children are his gift: he opens the womb, and Rachel is barren, as Sarah and Rebekah had been (11:30; 25:21).

decisions.choice: unloved
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the word in this setting (m1); Literal keeps "hated".

decisions.choice: he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the LORD.

records.source: וַתַּ֤הַר לֵאָה֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ רְאוּבֵ֑ן כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֗ה כִּֽי־רָאָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּעָנְיִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה יֶאֱהָבַ֥נִי אִישִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: And conceived Leah and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben, for she said, because has looked YHWH on my affliction; for now will love me my husband.
pieces: Leah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Reuben, saying, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has seen how I suffer. Surely now my husband will love me."

L.32: And Leah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben, for she said, "Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has looked on my affliction; for now my husband will love me."

R.32: Leah became pregnant and had a son. She named him Reuben, which sounds like "He has seen my trouble." She said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has seen how unhappy I am. Now my husband will surely love me."

decisions.choice: Reuben: "look, a son", heard as "he has seen my affliction"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like re'u ben, "look, a son". Leah hears in it ra'ah be'onyi, "the LORD has seen my affliction". Hagar had named her well for the God who sees (16:11-14).

decisions.choice: my affliction ('oni): misery, humiliation
decisions.reason: The word is used of Hagar's misery (16:11) and of Israel's suffering in Egypt (Exodus 3:7).

decisions.choice: now my husband will love me: a hope not met
decisions.reason: Leah hopes a son will win Jacob's love. Her words with each son show how far the hope is from coming true (verses 33-34).

decisions.choice: which sounds like "He has seen my trouble"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay on the name (m1).

records.source: וַתַּ֣הַר עוֹד֮ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּן֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־שְׂנוּאָ֣ה אָנֹ֔כִי וַיִּתֶּן־לִ֖י גַּם־אֶת־זֶ֑ה וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And she conceived again and bore a son and said, because has heard YHWH that hated [am] I, and he has given me also this one; and she called his name Simeon.
pieces: She conceived again and had another son. "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has heard that I am unloved," she said, "and so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given me this son as well." So she named him Simeon.

L.33: And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, "Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has heard that I am hated, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given me this one also." And she called his name Simeon.

R.33: Leah became pregnant again and had another son. She said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} heard that my husband does not love me, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave me this son too." She named him Simeon, which sounds like "he heard."

decisions.choice: Simeon: from shama, "he has heard"
decisions.reason: The name Shim'on sounds like the verb "to hear". God hears the cry of the unloved, as he heard Hagar (16:11; 21:17).

decisions.choice: which sounds like "he heard"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay on the name (m1).

decisions.choice: he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the LORD.

records.source: וַתַּ֣הַר עוֹד֮ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּן֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר עַתָּ֤ה הַפַּ֨עַם֙ יִלָּוֶ֤ה אִישִׁי֙ אֵלַ֔י כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים עַל־כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־שְׁמ֖וֹ לֵוִֽי׃
records.gloss: And she conceived again and bore a son and said, now this time will be joined my husband to me, for I have borne to him three sons; therefore he called his name Levi.
pieces: Once more she conceived and had a son. "Now at last my husband will become attached to me," she said, "because I have given him three sons." That is why he was named Levi.

L.34: And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, "Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons." Therefore he called his name Levi.

R.34: Leah became pregnant again and had another son. She said, "Now at last my husband will feel close to me, because I have given him three sons." So he was named Levi, which sounds like "joined."

decisions.choice: will be joined (yillaweh): Levi, "joined"
decisions.reason: The verb lavah means to be joined or attached; the name Levi sounds like it. Later the tribe of Levi was "joined" to Aaron to serve at the tabernacle (Numbers 18:2, 4).

decisions.choice: he called his name: the Hebrew has "he", not "she"
alternatives: she called his name (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint)
decisions.reason: With the other sons Leah names the child (verses 32, 33, 35). Here the Hebrew says "he called", which may mean Jacob, or simply "one called", that is, "he was named". The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read "she called". The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: he was named
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the verb as impersonal (m2).

decisions.choice: which sounds like "joined"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay on the name (m1).

records.source: וַתַּ֨הַר ע֜וֹד וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֗ן וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַפַּ֨עַם֙ אוֹדֶ֣ה אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה עַל־כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד מִלֶּֽדֶת׃
records.gloss: And she conceived again and bore a son and said, this time I will praise YHWH; therefore she called his name Judah. And she stopped from bearing.
pieces: She conceived yet again and gave birth to a son. "Now I will give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," she said, and so she named him Judah. Then for a time she had no more children.

L.35: And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, "This time I will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." Therefore she called his name Judah. And she ceased bearing.

R.35: Leah became pregnant again and had another son. She said, "Now I will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." So she named him Judah, which sounds like "praise." After that, Leah stopped having children for a while.

decisions.choice: Judah: from odeh, "I will praise"
decisions.reason: The name Yehudah sounds like the verb "praise, give thanks" (yadah). Jacob plays on it again in his blessing: "Judah, your brothers shall praise you" (49:8).

decisions.choice: this time I will praise the LORD: Leah's words change
decisions.reason: With her first three sons Leah spoke of her husband's love; now she speaks only of praising God. From Judah came David's royal line and, in the New Testament, Jesus (Matthew 1:2-16).

decisions.choice: she ceased bearing: for a time
decisions.reason: Leah later bears two more sons and a daughter (30:17-21). The pause sets up the next stage of the sisters' rivalry.

decisions.choice: which sounds like "praise"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay on the name (m1).

decisions.choice: for a time (B); for a while (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear the pause was not permanent (m3).
